offence_severity: 302, 307, 120B, 23, 114 IPC, Sections 3, 25(1B)(a), 5, 27 of the Arms Act and Sections 3(2)(i), 3(2(ii), 3(3), 3(5), 5, 6 of TADA Act
number_of_offences: Number of offences/counts charged and how many were finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The court accepted that the approver, Riyaz Ahmed Siddique, had been granted conditional pardon under Section 307 Cr.P.C. for making full and true disclosure of the facts concerning the murder of Pradeep Jain. However, upon the Public Prosecutor issuing a certificate under Section 308 Cr.P.C. that he had not complied with the condition, the court held that he was reverted to the position of an accused and his evidence was rendered useless for the trial of the co-accused.
witness_credibility: The court assessed that the approver, once his pardon was forfeited, was relegated to the position of an accused and thus his evidence was not considered credible for the purposes of the trial of the co-accused. The court also noted that the evidence of an accomplice is generally unworthy of credit unless corroborated, as per Section 114 of the Evidence Act.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: March 7, 1995; Trial judgment: July 11, 2001; High Court decision: Not stated; Supreme Court decision: October 5, 2010
legal_representation: Arun Pednekar, Sanjay V. Kharde and Asha Gopalan Nair for the Appellant; Rishi Malhotra, Mrinmayee Sahu and Shivaji M. Jadhav for the Respondents
investigation_status: Charge sheet filed: April 28, 2006; Trial completed: Not stated
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquittal of accused on August 5, 1997; High Court: Partly set aside on July 11, 2001; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed on October 5, 2010
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that once the pardon was forfeited on a certificate given by the public prosecutor under Section 308 Cr.P.C., the approver was relegated to the position of an accused and his evidence could not be used for any purpose. The prosecution also emphasized that the approver's evidence should not be used in the trial of the co-accused.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the withdrawal of pardon by the public prosecutor did not automatically strip the approver of his status as a witness. They contended that the evidence recorded by the court should not be disregarded and that the accused had a statutory right to cross-examine the approver, even if he was no longer supporting the prosecution.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that once an accomplice is granted pardon under Sections 306 or 307 Cr.P.C., he becomes a witness for the prosecution. However, if the pardon is forfeited on a certificate under Section 308 Cr.P.C., the approver is reverted to the position of an accused and his evidence is rendered useless for the purposes of the trial of the co-accused.
precedent_relied_upon: A.J. Peiris v. State of Madras AIR 1954 SC 616; State v. Hiralal Girdharila/ Kothari AIR 1960 SC 360; State (Delhi Administration) v. Jagjit Sing 1989 Supp (2) SCC 770
